The screen now collects and shows the icon and preview image. Refresh **http://maker:4001** and let's walk through it.

A note on what's real vs simulated here, so you're not misled: in this prototype the **favicon is fetched live** from each site (so you'll see real icons when your browser has internet), while the **preview image is a stand-in thumbnail** representing the page's real preview — the *behaviour* is what we're confirming, not the actual images.

A couple of decisions I made, to judge:
- I show the **preview image beneath the fetched details** while saving, and a **thumbnail on the right of each saved bookmark**.
- When a page offers **no preview image**, I show a quiet *"No preview image available"* rather than an empty gap.
- The **icon falls back to the coloured letter** if a site's real icon can't be loaded.

**Please try this:**

1. Paste `https://example.com`. Alongside the fetched title/description, confirm you now see the **site's icon** and a **preview image** (the stand-in thumbnail). Save it, and confirm the saved row shows the **icon** and a **thumbnail**.
2. Paste a link I've set up to have **no preview image**: `https://noimage.example`. Confirm you get the calm *"No preview image available"* line instead of a blank space — and it's still fully saveable.
3. Click **"Add 12 sample bookmarks"** and confirm icons and thumbnails appear across the list (a few samples deliberately have no thumbnail, to show that case too).

Tell me: does having the **icon and a preview image collected automatically and shown per bookmark** — with a graceful fallback when there's no image — match what you expected? And is the **thumbnail-on-the-right** placement in the list what you had in mind, or would you picture it differently?
